page: Microsoft Azure FX16mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 336.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 21.0 GB per core. The server includes 945 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the processor demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds fall within the top 25% tier. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally align with the middle 50% average. Notably, the PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25% tier, indicating a potential tradeoff in memory latency or throughput despite the large capacity.

Given the high memory density of 21.0 GB per core and the inclusion of 945 GB of local storage, this server is structured for memory-intensive workloads and database operations. The presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) supports workloads like low-latency LLM inference, where text generation for small models achieves top-tier performance. The hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not require GPU acceleration but need substantial RAM and high single-core CPU speeds.
